title: Initial POC: Telemetry Bench & Creds Gate
summary: Redwood and Hearthwell walked through the first telemetry bench results, identified a KV-cache contention pattern under concurrent synthetic load, confirmed credential provisioning progress and KMS integration timeline, and agreed on a tightened action list: run focused cache stress runs, finalize KMS key policy, and schedule a short canary test for read-only traffic next week.

Hearthwell to finish KMS role binding and confirm test keys (Ravi) by 2026-07-17
Liam to run targeted cache stress harness and provide results (Liam) by 2026-07-19

Ravi Singh: confirm KMS role binding & provide test key ARN (due 2026-07-17)

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-14
Start time: 16:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (Hearthwell - Head of ML), Emily Zhou (Platform Engineer), Ravi Singh (Security), Dina Park (SRE)

Optional auto sections present: Summary, Topics, Action items, Quick links
Shared links: https://redwood.ai/poc-telemetry (deck - shared by Maya), bench-csv (link: internal-drive/bench-raw.csv)

00:00 Maya: okay, hey everyone thanks for joining, let's do a quick 40-minute sync, I have the telemetry slices and then we can go into credentials and the cache stress, sound good?
00:12 Carlos: yeah that works, um we're mostly interested in the KV-cache numbers and the tail latency impact when we ramp to 500 qps, so, you know, the numbers you sent yesterday looked promising but we want the raw traces.
00:28 Liam: right, so quick note, the initial synthetic bench was run with our continuous-batcher at 256 sequence, and we saw a cluster of evicts around 120 seconds into the run — which is where the kv-cache, sometimes transcribed as "kv-cash" in the logs, started to show misses.
00:45 Emily: just to check, was that run with prefix caching enabled? we didn't enable our prefix pinning on the client side for that run.
00:52 Liam: correct, prefix pinning was off for the first bench; we wanted to see cold-start dynamics. When we re-ran with client-side prefix pinning on, the miss rate dropped ~35% but the tail p95 didn't move as much as we'd hoped.
01:09 Carlos: hmm, so delta in token cost looks good but tail latency is still a problem. did you capture KV cache hits per key size? the traces we saw had large variation.
01:20 Liam: yep i exported the per-key distribution, it's in the bench CSV. note though the instrumentation at the time stamped some rows with timezone shifts which caused a small misalignment — we'll clean that.
01:34 Maya: quick interjection — Ravi, are you on the KMS path? we saw a partial key ARN earlier in the provisioning notes.
01:41 Ravi: yes, so I got the bind request from your docs, I created the role, but there was a small IAM policy quirk: the kms:Decrypt permission wasn't scoped to the test key, so our security team asked to narrow it. I'll update and send the ARN.
01:55 Dina: also, regarding network egress, we need to confirm the private gateway IPs again; last time we had a mismatch and the canary failed during the egress check.
02:06 Maya: noted, we'll re-send the gateway list.
02:10 Carlos: can we talk about the telemetry sampling briefly — you're collecting token-level traces at 10% sampling right now? that might miss the pathological tail events.
02:19 Liam: We're sampling at adaptive 10% by default, increasing to 50% for the stress harness. For production you probably want to keep sampling low, but for root-cause on the p95 we can bump it.
02:33 Emily: any concerns about cost when bumping to 50% for a few runs? our finance team will ask.
02:38 Maya: it's a short experiment window; we'll mark it as scoped to the bench and export only the relevant timestamps so cost impact is contained.
02:47 Carlos: ok great.
03:02 Liam: on the cache contention, we hypothesize three contributing factors: 1) shard imbalance under parallelism, 2) eviction policy interacting poorly with varied prefix lengths, and 3) transient I/O backpressure during long sequences. We saw the eviction spike align with a GC-like pause in the worker node logs.
03:22 Emily: GC pause? that's surprising, what runtime are you seeing that on? our infra team's JVM settings are tuned but we use a mix of runtimes.
03:30 Liam: it's in the inference-worker container; can be a mix of Python GC and a native allocator pause. the logs show stall windows of 60-120 ms.
03:41 Carlos: is that something Redwood has a patch for? like a kernel param or runtime flag?
03:46 Liam: we have two mitigations: adjust worker thread affinity and increase the prefetch window for KV cache. We'll test both in the stress harness tomorrow.
03:55 Maya: we'll add that as an action.
04:01 Ravi: on security, once you push the updated IAM policy narrow to the key, can you also share the audit log locations? we need to map them to our SIEM.
04:10 Maya: yes, Redwood supports audit exports to S3 and can forward CloudTrail-style events, we'll send the doc link.
04:18 Ravi: perfect.
04:25 Carlos: what about the planned canary traffic pattern, are we doing read-only first? we want to avoid anything that might write or mutate LLM state.
04:33 Maya: agreed, canary will be read-only; Dina will coordinate the window, and we want a 30m run at steady 100 qps then spike to 300 qps for 5 minutes to observe tail.
04:46 Dina: that's fine, I'll coordinate with oncall and post runbook.
05:00 Liam: small note — when we ran a similar canary on another pilot, we had a fallback where the router switched models to a lower-memory variant automatically; do you want that behavior here?
05:12 Carlos: probably yes, but we need to understand the quality impact. could you share a short A/B sample of model outputs for the lower-memory variant?
05:20 Maya: yep we'll attach a 20-sample A/B in the telemetry package.
05:27 Emily: earlier you mentioned the continuous-batcher config, can you expose the batching window and max-batch-size used in the bench?
05:33 Liam: sure: window=12ms, max_batch=64, kv_prefetch=2. We'll include exact config in the CSV header, but note we changed kv_prefetch to 4 in the second run.
05:46 Carlos: good. quick question about retention: how long will Redwood keep the raw token traces? we don't want PII leaking or more retention than necessary.
05:56 Maya: by default bench artifacts are kept 14 days, but for enterprise pilots you can set retention to 7 or even 3 days while we operate. we can set a short retention for this project.
06:06 Ravi: that's acceptable, and please ensure logs in S3 are encrypted with our KMS key.
06:12 Maya: understood. we'll wire that into the handoff doc.
06:19 Liam: final technical point — the bench CSV shows a small number of malformed rows where model name was "redwood-lmr-v2" but sometimes transcribed as "red-wood lmr v2" in the exporter; it's cosmetic but we're fixing the exporter to standardize names.
06:34 Carlos: ok makes parsing easier.
06:40 Maya: quick recap and owners: Maya will share telemetry trimmed dashboard + raw CSV by 7/16; Ravi to confirm KMS key and tightened IAM by 7/17; Liam to run focused KV cache stress by 7/19; Dina to schedule canary and runbook by 7/20.
06:58 Carlos: sounds good, one more ask: can you include the bench seed and randomization so we can reproduce?
07:05 Liam: yes the bench seed is in the config and we'll export the harness command line.
07:12 Emily: we'll try to have the infra ready for the 7/20 canary, I might need a short troubleshooting window with Redwood during the run.
07:20 Maya: we'll be on call for the canary, and we'll prepare a runbook and rollback play.
07:25 Ravi: okay thanks everyone.
07:30 Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread and I'll make sure the artifacts are in the shared folder.
07:36 Meeting end

Notes on transcription: occasional mis-attribs (Speaker 2 labelled as Liam sometimes), filler words, and minor recognition errors (kv-cash, red-wood).
